description: Gripper 3.x: build the base/drive assembly that the grippers attach to. From the key reference photo (cad/reference/generalist_gripper_gen6_closed.png and references/generalist): the black handles extend back behind the yellow fingers, wrap around, and connect into a common base. A single motor is mounted underneath that base; it spins and drives gears attached to the black handles, which opens and closes the gripper. Model the base, the motor mount (single motor underneath) and the gear linkage to the handles. Fully parameterized: add every dimension to params.json with docs and slider ranges so it appears in the live preview Tune panel. Must be swappable with any handle version: define a common handle-to-base interface so any 2.x handle fits. Every piece separable, each its own module and its own STL. Motor (Jake's corrections, replacing the SO-101 STS3215 and then the Damiao DM-J4310-2EC): the RobStride RS00, the gripper motor of Seeed's reBot Arm B601-RS (4x RS00 + 3x RS06; LeRobot follower lerobot-robot-seeed-b601 seeed_b601_rs_follower.py names the gripper rs-00). Size the mount from RobStride's RS00 drawing (Seeed 100083284) and RS00.step: 57 mm x 51 mm body, 35 mm output boss, output 6x M3 on 27 mm, front ring 6x M3 + 2 dowels on 50 mm, back 4x M3 on 38 mm. Make every motor dimension a params.json entry. This starts the new 3.x line (gripper plus handles plus base) per AGENTS.md.

results.identified_issue:
Motor history: description said SO-101 STS3215; Jake's first mid-turn correction said Damiao DM-J4310-2EC (B601-DM gripper); a second mid-turn message arrived truncated (started mid-URL) listing the B601-RS follower file, BOM 4x RS00 + 3x RS06, the RS00 drawing/STEP/manual, and said "also recorded in plans/aero_hand_on_b601.md on main" (not on origin/main when checked). I read it as superseding the DM choice: the RS follower config names the gripper "rs-00". If Jake meant DM-J4310 after all, only the "Motor" param group values change: DM-J4310-2EC per its manual drawing is 57 x 46 body (45 + 1 boss), output boss 35, 6x M3 on 27 output (3x dia 4 pins on 24.3), 6x M3 + 2x dia 3 dowels on 50 front, 4x M3 depth 4 on 38 back — nearly the same pattern, so motor_len 51 -> 45 is the main change.
Design: drive stacks down the ventral (-y) side under the 2.6 handle plates (y -18.5): arm floor, gear, base, motor. Gears: pitch radius = pivot (derived; gear_teeth sets module), left gear half-tooth phase. Motor coaxial with right pivot (direct drive like v005) instead of a central pinion (would turn both gears the same way). Interface screws at iface_screw_phase 0 sit under finger material at x=-8, so assembly order is arm onto gear first, then finger+handle unit dropped into the channel (checked). Rejected: pinning the finger at the pivot (finger stub around origin is only ~3 mm wall) and a cup round the finger base (conflicts with the handle plate's foot).
Not verified: tooth strength, plastic bushing for the left gear, no axial retention, no swing stops, the RS00 second dowel's position (assumed opposite), the wrist pattern. check_geometry's new drive checks use the Manifold backend for speed. Removed copied 2.6 compare_web_stl.md / compare_v205.png from the new folder as stale.
results.summary: Built gripper 3.1: 2.6's fingers and handles on a common base, with two meshing gears driven by one RobStride RS00 underneath.
results.detailed_description:
New folder v301_generalist_base. Under each handle sits a black arm: a channel grips the handle plate's bottom edge, which also stops the handle sliding back out, and a floor runs from there to a hub on the finger's pivot. Each arm drops a 10 mm hex boss (plus two M3 screws) into a gear. That hex joint is the shared handle-to-base interface: to use another 2.x handle, print an arm from that handle's params, and the gears, base and motor stay the same.

The two gears are equal involute sectors that mesh on the centreline, so the fingers swing 1:1 in opposite directions. Under them is one black base plate with a wrist tab. I used the RS00 from your second message, since that's the B601-RS gripper motor. It sits under the right pivot (so the motor is off-centre) and bolts to the plate on its 50 mm ring; its 27 mm output flange bolts to the right gear, and the left gear follows through the mesh. Every RS00 number comes from its drawing and STEP and is in params.json; 52 new sliders in all. The pebble description now says RS00.

All checks pass, including the gears meshing clear at every degree from 0 to 30 and nothing hitting the base or motor. Not printed, and no RS00 in hand. The wrist holes are placeholders, and the fingers have no pivot pin (each is held only through its handle). Your second message reached me cut off at the start, so tell me if RS00 wasn't the point.

summary: Model the gripper 3.x base with a single underneath motor mount sized for the SO-101's STS3215 servo, plus gears linking to the handles. Make every dimension tunable in params.json, give each part its own STL, and define a common interface so any 2.x handle fits.
